body: ## Purpose
How solutions engineers estimate a prospect's monthly tokens before a quote. Estimates use an approximate tokenizer and round up 10% for safety. This page is about forecasting before purchase. It does not explain how billed tokens are counted on an invoice; for that, see the token accounting pages and the billing routing page.
## Method
1. Sample 100 representative requests.
2. Count characters and divide by 4 for English text.
3. Multiply by expected monthly volume and add 10%.

Operational runbook (support-facing quick steps):
1) When a customer reports \"quota exceeded\":
   a) Ask for request-id or approximate timestamp and route.
   b) Check per-account bucket state in Admin Console -> Usage -> Buckets.
   c) Pull request audit log and reconcile estimated vs actual CR.

- Direct Redwood invoices for Hosted API, Embeddings, Batch and Dedicated.
- Marketplace purchases are out of scope: adjustments go through the marketplace (see the marketplace invoicing notes).
- Contracted Enterprise accounts follow this matrix unless their order form names a different approver.
## Definitions
- **Adjustment**: any change to what a customer owes after an invoice is issued: a credit note, a refund, a write-off or a re-issued invoice.
- **Per line**: the amount of one invoice line, taken whole. An adjustment is never split across several smaller ones to stay under a limit.
- **Billing error**: a line that bills the wrong rate, quantity or product, or bills the same usage twice.
- **Goodwill**: any reduction of a correct charge, for any reason."}, {"source": "sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-556901-cache-hit-invoice-line-explanation-and-provisional-credit.json", "chunk": "3/7", "kind": "Jira ticket", "title": "SUP-556901: Invoice shows separate 'cache-hit tokens' line plus 'generated tokens' for same time window — clarification and potential adjustment requested", "status": "In Progress", "date": "2026-03-03", "text": "  - 2) Run a 3-day batch of repeated prompt variants that should hit the cache ~65% of the time, and record tokens generated vs. returned from cache in the runtime metrics console.

- VectorAI Labs noticed ~0.6% higher token consumption on invoice lines for two billing days (2026-03-09 to 2026-03-10).
- Missing provisional credit prevented automatic mid-cycle correction; customer autopay charged the higher amount.
- Customer workload is production-critical; they flagged for finance reconciliation and requested a credit memo.

Actual behavior:"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/token-accounting-discrepancy-intake-and-triage.json", "chunk": "3/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Ops: Reconciling token accounting discrepancy reports (intake + triage)", "status": "published", "date": "2025-04-22", "text": "## How to avoid double counting
1. If a report arrives in Slack or Gmail, file a SUP ticket and link it.
2. Mark the SUP ticket label `token-accounting` and add the origin channel in the description (Slack/Gmail).
3. In weekly reporting, count the case by *origin* (Slack vs Gmail vs Jira), not by total artifacts.
## Common root causes to check
- Streaming retries/reconnect (tokens can be emitted twice)
- Client counts only final chunk tokens
- Different tokenizer / unicode normalization
- Whitespace/newlines included in input strings
- Tool-call serialization adds tokens
- Prefix-cache billing bug (rare; see SUP-3009)"}]}
